issues.legal_issue: A conviction based on circumstantial evidence cannot stand unless each circumstance is established beyond doubt and the circumstances together point only to guilt.
material_facts: There was no eyewitness to the killing.
The accused was seen with the deceased on the evening before the deceased was found dead, and the accused admitted being with him.
Clothing recovered from the accused bore human blood, but the evidence did not connect that blood to the deceased.

The alleged confession was made after a long interval; one of the two witnesses denied that it had been made, and it was allegedly made in circumstances in which the accused was seeking to avoid being handed to police.
A different person had a land dispute and grudge against the deceased, and the alleged weapon was recovered at that person’s instance; that person was discharged.
The accused’s presence with the deceased was the only circumstance the Court regarded as established.
issues.conclusion: The established circumstances did not prove guilt beyond doubt; the conviction and sentence were set aside and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: For circumstantial evidence, each circumstance must be established beyond doubt and the circumstances cumulatively must lead only to the inference of guilt. The Court applied this principle in considering the conviction under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code and the evidentiary principles identified under Sections 3 and 14 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. No earlier case is relied on in the judgment.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_circumstantial_c: The accused appealed a criminal conviction that rested on circumstantial evidence.
predicates.last_seen_is_only_established_circumstan: The accused was seen with the deceased before the death, but no other circumstance was established as incriminating.
predicates.blood_evidence_does_not_link_to_deceased: Blood on clothing attributed to the accused was not scientifically linked to the deceased.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a circumstantial conviction and the established evidence consists of the accused being last seen with the deceased while the blood evidence and alleged confession do not provide reliable links, particularly where another person had a motive and the weapon was recovered from that person, the conviction is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: Human blood on clothing does not connect the clothing to a deceased person when the evidence does not identify the blood group or otherwise establish that connection.
material_facts: A shirt and dhoti recovered from the accused were reported to have human blood stains.
The serologist’s report did not identify the blood group, so the stains could not be positively connected to the deceased.
The evidence did not clearly establish that the accused wore the dhoti at the time of the incident, and the stains could have been the accused’s own blood.
issues.conclusion: The blood stains could not support an inference connecting the accused or the clothing to the deceased or the offence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the clothing evidence under the evidentiary principles identified in Sections 3 and 14 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, and held that human blood without evidence connecting it to the deceased was not a basis for the required inference. No earlier case is relied on in the judgment.

issues.definition: If a circumstantial prosecution relies on clothing bearing human blood but the evidence does not connect that blood to the deceased, the clothing does not link the accused to the deceased.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged extra-judicial confession is not reliable where its circumstances are doubtful, it is made after a long interval, and a supporting witness denies it.
material_facts: The alleged confession was said to have been made years after the killing, when the accused was apprehended in another matter and produced before a village head.
The accused allegedly said he was wanted in a murder case and asked not to be handed over to police before allegedly confessing.
One of the two witnesses to the alleged confession denied in cross-examination that the accused had made it.
issues.conclusion: The alleged confession could not be relied on and had to be left out of consideration.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the confession on the reliability of its proof and the circumstances in which it was allegedly made. It applied the evidentiary principles identified under Sections 3 and 14 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. No earlier case is relied on in the judgment.

predicates.alleged_extra_judicial_confession: A witness claims that the accused confessed outside court.
predicates.confession_made_after_long_interval: The alleged confession was made a substantial time after the event under investigation.

issues.definition: When a circumstantial prosecution relies on a delayed alleged confession that a supporting witness denies and whose circumstances are doubtful, the confession cannot be relied on.
